fields.claim_quote: for any word $\sigma^\prime\in \left(2^{\Xi} \right)^{\omega}$ such that $\hat\sigma$ is a prefix of $\sigma^\prime$, we have that $\sigma^\prime,i \not \Vdash(P1E \wedge P2E) \rightarrow  (\mathsf{F}\, (P1C \vee P2C))$
fields.explanation: The truth of F(P1C OR P2C) at position i depends on future letters that a finite prefix does not fix. In the concrete witness, adding P1C at time1 repairs the violation at0 without changing its one-letter prefix. More generally, any finite prefix of length L can be followed by {P1C} forever: each antecedent position in the prefix has a future P1C at L, and all later antecedents are false. This directly proves every finite prefix is extendible to a satisfying word. The selected theorem certifies the concrete infinite-word counterexample; it does not certify historical sweep counts or runtime.
fields.flaw: In the safety-property argument, the author claims that any extension σ' of the finite prefix σ̂ = σ[..i] still violates the implication at position i, i.e., σ',i ⊭ (P1E ∧ P2E) → F(P1C ∨ P2C), so σ̂ is a bad prefix. This is false: satisfaction of F(P1C ∨ P2C) at position i depends on the infinite suffix beyond the prefix, so an extension can repair the violation.
fields.source_context:
0001 | I have to prove whether a certain property is safety or liveliness. The property represents the absence of deadlock so I expected it to be a safety property from what I read online. 
0002 | 
0003 | 
0004 | The issue is that I seem to show that it is both, but this is impossible as the only property that is both safety and liveliness would be $\left(2^{\Xi}\right)^{\omega}$, where $\Xi$ is the set of propositional symbols. I would like to understand where the mistake is, and naturally if any of the solutions would be correct. Also, I would like to do it in a formal way instead of using the "something bad never happens" intuitive idea.
0005 | 
0006 | \
0007 | The property in question is: $$ \mathsf{G}((P1E \wedge P2E) \rightarrow  (\mathsf{F}\, (P1C \vee  P2C))) $$
0008 | 
0009 |  1. The definition I have for safety property goes as follows:
0010 | >An LT property $P_{safe}$ over $\Xi$ is called a safety property if for all words $\sigma \in\left(2^{\Xi}\right)^{\omega} \setminus P_{safe}$ there exists a finite prefix $\hat\sigma$ of $\sigma$ such that
0011 | $$P_{safe} \cap \{\sigma^\prime\in \left(2^{\Xi}\right)^{\omega}\; |\; \hat\sigma \textrm{ is a finite prefix of }\sigma^\prime
0012 | \} = \emptyset $$
0013 | 
0014 | What I tried to do is as follows:
0015 | 
0016 | Let $\sigma\in \left(2^{\Xi} \right)^{\omega}$ be an arbitrary word such that $\sigma\not \Vdash \mathsf{G}((P1E \wedge P2E) \rightarrow  (\mathsf{F}\, (P1C \vee P2C))) $, then there exists $i\geq 0$ such that $\sigma, i\,\not \Vdash (P1E \wedge P2E) \rightarrow  (\mathsf{F}\, (P1C \vee P2C)) $. Let $\hat\sigma=\sigma[..i]$, this is a bad prefix of $\sigma$, and for any word $\sigma^\prime\in \left(2^{\Xi} \right)^{\omega}$ such that $\hat\sigma$ is a prefix of $\sigma^\prime$, we have that $\sigma^\prime,i \not \Vdash(P1E \wedge P2E) \rightarrow  (\mathsf{F}\, (P1C \vee P2C))$, thus:
0017 |     $\sigma^\prime\not \Vdash \mathsf{G}((P1E \wedge P2E) \rightarrow  (\mathsf{F}\, ( P1C \vee P2C))) $. We conclude it is a **safety property**.
0018 |
fields.witness: Use Xi={P1E,P2E,P1C,P2C}. Let sigma(0)={P1E,P2E} and sigma(t)=empty for t>0. It violates the response implication at0. Its one-letter prefix sigma[..0] also prefixes sigmaPrime, where sigmaPrime(0)={P1E,P2E} and sigmaPrime(t)={P1C} for t>0. The eventuality at0 is fulfilled at1, and later antecedents are false, so sigmaPrime satisfies the full global formula. Thus the proposed prefix is not bad. The selected Lean theorem proves these statements for functions Nat->Letter.
